notable.note: The only call in this batch where money changed hands, and it was not the programme. Facing a prospect who had just said the price was higher than expected and that he would not commit until he knew he could finish, the rep introduced a $100 deposit — a mechanism that appears nowhere in the stated offer — justified it on calendar scarcity ('our calendar is so full, instead of having to take someone else to have a meeting with'), promised verbally that it was returnable, invoiced it live and collected it. Note also that the same rep, on this same day, told a prospect on disability income that the company 'can only split up into six payments' with added interest, while offering this prospect three payments at list price. Clinically, the prospect disclosed an unnamed chronic intestinal condition at minute three, said explicitly 'I cannot go like too hard', and was then sold three to four high-intensity sessions a week plus a time-restricted eating protocol; the condition was never named, never revisited and no clinician was mentioned.
